```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6
)
library(SpaceMosaic)
library(HDF5Array)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
```

# Aim

The [patch diagnostics vignette](patch_diagnostics.Rmd) shows that patch
assignments change with the random seed. Here we ask how this affects
differential expression (DE) and meta analysis. We use the immune surveillance
example from the [`mouse_colon` vignette](mouse_colon.Rmd) and run the full
analysis with ten random seeds. All other settings are fixed, and
`getPatches()` uses the default 15 iterations.

## Questions

1. **Patches.** How similar are the patch assignments across seeds (ARI)?
2. **Genes.** Do the same genes come out on top? Do their maps look alike?
3. **Raw vs meta Z.** `patchDE()` gives a raw Z score per gene and patch.
   `patchMetaAnalysis()` combines each patch with its neighbor patches and
   gives a meta Z score. Is the variation across seeds already present in raw
   Z, or is it added by the meta analysis?
4. **Ensemble.** Can we combine the seeds into one more stable map?
5. **Null.** How many $|Z| > 2$ pairs do we get when X is unrelated to
   expression?

## Take-home messages

- Patch assignments are similar across seeds, with some differences. Strong
  genes, such as `Axin2` and `Irf8`, are found in every run and in similar
  places.
- Weaker genes can change a lot between seeds. In the most variable gene, one
  run has a single patch with a very large raw Z. The meta analysis spreads it
  to the neighboring patches, so many patches get a large meta Z in that run.
- Meta Z gives more $|Z| > 2$ pairs than raw Z. The meta analysis gives a
  similar increase in the null runs, so part of this increase comes from the
  method itself.
- In the null with a rotated immune pattern, the fraction of $|Z| > 2$ pairs is
  similar to the real data. A significance test for an immune effect therefore
  needs a null reference, such as Z scores calibrated against null runs.
- The ensemble across seeds (median Z) removes run-specific patterns. The
  calibration question above applies to it as well.

# Data and settings

```{r data}
h5_path <- system.file("extdata", "mouse_colon", package = "SpaceMosaic")
spe <- HDF5Array::loadHDF5SummarizedExperiment(h5_path)
xy <- spatialCoords(spe)
rownames(xy) <- as.character(spe$cell_id)
cell_types <- spe$tier1
use <- cell_types == "Epithelial"
is_immune <- cell_types == "Immune"

# Compute the same neighborhood embedding and predictor for every seed.
Z <- embedCellNeighborhoods(reducedDim(spe, "PCA"), xy, ks = c(5, 50))
nn <- FNN::get.knn(as.matrix(xy), k = 100)$nn.index
X <- apply(nn, 1, function(i) sum(is_immune[i]))

xy_use <- as.matrix(xy[use, , drop = FALSE])
Z_use <- Z[use, , drop = FALSE]
X_use <- X[use]
counts <- assay(spe, "counts")[, use, drop = FALSE]
y <- t(counts)  # cells x genes
rownames(y) <- rownames(xy_use)
colnames(y) <- rownames(spe)
tot <- colSums(counts)
stopifnot(nrow(y) == nrow(xy_use), nrow(Z_use) == nrow(y),
          length(X_use) == nrow(y), length(tot) == nrow(y))

# Use the same thresholds across seeds.
dist_to_immune <- FNN::get.knnx(
  data = as.matrix(xy[is_immune, , drop = FALSE]),
  query = xy_use, k = 1
)$nn.dist[, 1]
log_tot <- log2(tot + 1)
seeds <- c(1, 7, 42, 101, 123, 777, 2024, 2025, 31415, 271828)
npatches <- 100; n_iters <- 15
min_cells <- 50; min_x_sd <- 0.5; min_stability <- 0.7
dist_thresh <- 15; count_thresh <- 6.65
```

We calculate patch diagnostics for every seed, and then
apply the same filtering thresholds as Scenario 1 in `mouse_colon.Rmd`.
Unassigned cells and filtered patches are excluded from DE.

```{r patch-runs}
runs <- patch_data <- vector("list", length(seeds))
names(runs) <- names(patch_data) <- as.character(seeds)
run_info <- vector("list", length(seeds))

for (i in seq_along(seeds)) {
  seed <- seeds[i]
  key <- as.character(seed)
  # Build patches and collect their diagnostics.
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- getPatches(
    xy = xy_use, X = X_use, Z = Z_use,
    npatches = npatches, n_iters = n_iters,
    log_iters = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
  )
  runs[[key]] <- fit$patch
  diag <- getPatchDiagnostics(xy = xy_use, X = X_use, patches = fit)
  pd <- diag$patch_diagnostics

  # Add the two filtering measures.
  pd$min_dist <- as.numeric(
    tapply(dist_to_immune, fit$patch, min)[as.character(pd$patch)]
  )
  pd$mean_counts <- as.numeric(
    tapply(log_tot, fit$patch, mean)[as.character(pd$patch)]
  )
  patch_data[[key]] <- pd
  # Keep a brief run summary.
  run_info[[i]] <- data.frame(
    seed = seed,
    patches = diag$assignment_summary$n_nonempty_patches,
    assigned = diag$assignment_summary$fraction_assigned
  )
}
```

```{r plot-data, include=FALSE}
plot_data <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(pd, seed) {
  pd$seed <- seed
  pd
}, patch_data, as.character(seeds)))
plot_data$seed <- factor(plot_data$seed, levels = as.character(seeds))
facet_theme <- theme_classic() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey65", fill = NA))
```

## Patch diagnostics before filtering {.tabset}

The tabs show patch properties across seeds. Red lines mark the thresholds
used below.

  geom_vline(xintercept = dist_thresh, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~seed, ncol = 5) +

## Filtering and DE

We apply the same thresholds in every run.

```{r de-runs}
filtered <- meta_z <- raw_z <- vector("list", length(seeds))
names(filtered) <- names(meta_z) <- names(raw_z) <- as.character(seeds)
for (i in seq_along(seeds)) {
  key <- as.character(seeds[i])
  pd <- patch_data[[key]]

  # Apply the Scenario 1 patch filters.
  keep <- with(pd, patch[
    mean_counts > count_thresh & min_dist < dist_thresh &
      n_cells >= min_cells & is.finite(x_sd) & x_sd >= min_x_sd &
      !is.na(membership_stability) & membership_stability >= min_stability
  ])
  patch <- runs[[key]]
  patch[!(patch %in% keep)] <- NA
  filtered[[key]] <- patch
  stopifnot(length(keep) >= 2)

  # Run DE and meta analysis for this patch set.
  de <- patchDE(
    y = y, df = data.frame(X = X_use), patch = patch,
    pearson = TRUE, tot = tot, verbose = FALSE
  )
  W <- getPatchAttributes(Z = Z_use, patch = patch)
  meta <- patchMetaAnalysis(DEobj = de, W = W, k = 10)
  meta_z[[key]] <- meta$X$ests / meta$X$ses
  # Keep the per-patch DE Z scores before meta analysis.
  raw_z[[key]] <- de$X$ests[, colnames(meta_z[[key]]), drop = FALSE] /
    de$X$ses[, colnames(meta_z[[key]]), drop = FALSE]

  run_info[[i]]$retained <- length(keep)
  run_info[[i]]$cells_for_DE <- sum(!is.na(patch))
}
run_info <- do.call(rbind, run_info)
run_info
```

Most patches pass the filters. On average, each run excludes
`r round(mean(run_info$patches - run_info$retained))` patches.

# Patch assignment agreement

Patch labels differ across runs. ARI compares which cells are grouped together,
independent of the patch labels. We show results before and after filtering.

```{r assignment-ari, fig.width=16, fig.height=9, fig.cap="ARI between seed pairs. The top row shows heatmaps on a fixed 0 to 1 color scale. The bottom row shows the 45 pair values. Before filtering is on the left."}
pairs <- combn(as.character(seeds), 2, simplify = FALSE)
ari <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(pair) {
  data.frame(seed1 = pair[1], seed2 = pair[2],
             before = mclust::adjustedRandIndex(runs[[pair[1]]], runs[[pair[2]]]),
             after = mclust::adjustedRandIndex(filtered[[pair[1]]], filtered[[pair[2]]]))
}))
ari_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(seed1 = ari$seed1, seed2 = ari$seed2,
             assignment = "Before filtering", ari = ari$before),
  data.frame(seed1 = ari$seed1, seed2 = ari$seed2,
             assignment = "After filtering", ari = ari$after)
)
ari_long$assignment <- factor(ari_long$assignment,
                              levels = c("Before filtering", "After filtering"))
diag_map <- expand.grid(seed = as.character(seeds),
                        assignment = c("Before filtering", "After filtering"))
diag_map$assignment <- factor(diag_map$assignment,
                              levels = levels(ari_long$assignment))
ari_map <- rbind(
  ari_long,
  data.frame(seed1 = ari_long$seed2, seed2 = ari_long$seed1,
             assignment = ari_long$assignment, ari = ari_long$ari),
  data.frame(seed1 = diag_map$seed, seed2 = diag_map$seed,
             assignment = diag_map$assignment, ari = 1)
)
stages <- levels(ari_long$assignment)
p_heat <- lapply(stages, function(stage) {
  ggplot(ari_map[ari_map$assignment == stage, ],
         aes(factor(seed1, levels = seeds), factor(seed2, levels = seeds),
             fill = ari)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ari), color = ari < 0.5),
              size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"),
                       guide = "none") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
    labs(title = stage, x = "Random seed", y = "Random seed", fill = "ARI")
})
p_hist <- lapply(stages, function(stage) {
  ggplot(ari_long[ari_long$assignment == stage, ], aes(ari)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025, fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = range(ari_long$ari)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "Pairwise ARI", y = "Number of seed pairs")
})
(wrap_plots(p_heat, ncol = 2) / wrap_plots(p_hist, ncol = 2)) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.5, 1), guides = "collect")
```

Filtering raises the mean ARI from `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(ari$before))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", mean(ari$after))`, and the median stays at
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(ari$before))`. Each filtered pair uses the cells
retained in both runs. In the following sections, we compare genes by name and
map patch results back to cells.

# DE and meta analysis agreement

`patchMetaAnalysis()` gives an estimate and a standard error for each gene in
each retained patch. We divide the estimate by its standard error to get a
$Z$ score. A positive score means expression rises with the number of nearby
immune cells. A negative score means expression falls. As in `mouse_colon.Rmd`,
we use $|Z| > 2$ to describe strong signals.

```{r de-counts}
# Count strong Z scores in each run.
de_counts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(seeds), function(i) {
  z <- meta_z[[i]]
  data.frame(
    seed = seeds[i], n_patches = ncol(z),
    n_pairs_Z2 = sum(abs(z) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_genes_Z2 = sum(rowSums(abs(z) > 2, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)
  )
}))
de_counts
```

Across runs, `r min(de_counts$n_pairs_Z2)` to
`r max(de_counts$n_pairs_Z2)` gene and patch pairs have $|Z| > 2$.
The number of genes with at least one such patch ranges from
`r min(de_counts$n_genes_Z2)` to `r max(de_counts$n_genes_Z2)`.
We next rank genes by the fraction of retained patches with $|Z| > 2$ in each
run.

```{r top-genes}
genes <- rownames(meta_z[[1]])
stopifnot(all(vapply(meta_z, function(z) identical(rownames(z), genes), logical(1))))

# Rank genes in each run and count top 50 appearances.
frac <- lapply(meta_z, function(z) {
  score <- rowMeans(abs(z) > 2, na.rm = TRUE)
  score[!is.finite(score)] <- NA_real_
  names(score) <- rownames(z)
  score
})
top50 <- lapply(frac, function(score) {
  head(names(score)[order(-score, names(score), na.last = TRUE)], 50)
})
top50_g <- rowSums(vapply(top50, function(x) genes %in% x,
                         logical(length(genes))))
frac_mat <- do.call(cbind, frac)

# Summarize positive and negative signals in each run.
up_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(meta_z, function(z) rowMeans(z > 2, na.rm = TRUE)))
down_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(meta_z, function(z) rowMeans(z < -2, na.rm = TRUE)))

# Take the median of each fraction across seeds.
gene_summary <- data.frame(
  gene = genes, top50_g = top50_g,
  median_fraction = apply(frac_mat, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  median_up = apply(up_mat, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  median_down = apply(down_mat, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
)
gene_summary <- gene_summary[
  order(-gene_summary$top50_g, -gene_summary$median_fraction,
        gene_summary$gene),
]
rownames(gene_summary) <- NULL
head(gene_summary, 20)
```

Each row is one gene. `top50_g` is the number of runs in which the gene is
among the top 50. `median_fraction` is the median, across runs, of the fraction
of retained patches with $|Z| > 2$. `median_up` and `median_down` are the same
median for $Z > 2$ and $Z < -2$. A gene can have both positive and negative
patches.
For `Axin2`, the median fractions are approximately `r round(100 * gene_summary$median_up[gene_summary$gene == "Axin2"])`% up and `r round(100 * gene_summary$median_down[gene_summary$gene == "Axin2"])`% down.

```{r top50-frequency, fig.cap="Frequency of each gene's inclusion among top 50 lists."}
ggplot(gene_summary[gene_summary$top50_g > 0, ], aes(top50_g)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#56B4E9") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(seeds)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Top 50 appearances across ten runs", y = "Number of genes")
```

In these runs, `r sum(gene_summary$top50_g == length(seeds))` genes appear in
the top 50 every time.

The next plot shows the up and down fractions for the ten genes that appear
most often in the top 50. For one gene in one run, the up fraction is the
fraction of retained patches with $Z > 2$, where expression rises with X. The
down fraction is the fraction with $Z < -2$, where expression falls with X.
Each point is one run. Flat lines mean the gene behaves the same in every run.

```{r directions, fig.width=16, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Fraction of patches with Z above 2 or below minus 2 for ten frequent top 50 genes."}
# Show each seed's directional fractions for recurrent genes.
top10 <- head(gene_summary$gene, 10)
idx <- match(top10, genes)
direction_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(seeds), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    gene = rep(top10, 2), seed = rep(as.character(seeds[i]), 2 * length(top10)),
    direction = rep(c("Up", "Down"), each = length(top10)),
    fraction = c(up_mat[idx, i], down_mat[idx, i])
  )
}))
direction_data$seed <- factor(direction_data$seed, levels = as.character(seeds))

ggplot(direction_data, aes(seed, fraction, color = direction,
                           group = direction)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~gene, ncol = 5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = "#D55E00", Down = "#0072B2")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Random seed", y = "Fraction of retained patches", color = NULL)
```

`Irf8` has mostly positive signals. `Tnfrsf21` has negative signals. `Nlrp9b`
has patches with both directions.

We first map `Axin2`, which appears in every top 50 list.
It has positive signals in similar areas across seeds. Patch boundaries
and Z scores vary within those areas.

```{r spatial-gene, fig.width=16, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Axin2 meta analysis Z scores across ten seeds. Grey cells were excluded from DE."}
# Map patch Z scores to the same cell coordinates.
gene_map <- function(gene, zlist = meta_z) {
  map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(zlist), function(seed) {
    patch <- filtered[[seed]]
    zmat <- zlist[[seed]]
    patch_col <- match(as.character(patch), colnames(zmat))
    stopifnot(all(!is.na(patch_col[!is.na(patch)])))
    data.frame(x = xy_use[, 1], y = xy_use[, 2], seed = seed,
               z = as.numeric(zmat[gene, patch_col]))
  }))
  map$seed <- factor(map$seed, levels = as.character(seeds))
  map
}
axin2_map <- gene_map("Axin2")
ggplot(axin2_map, aes(x, y, color = z)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~seed, ncol = 5) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = range(xy_use[, 1]), ylim = range(xy_use[, 2])) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "white", high = "#D55E00",
                        midpoint = 0, na.value = "grey80") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Axin2", color = "Meta Z")
```


We also look for genes that change more across seeds. The table includes genes
that enter the top 50 at least once. `min_frac` and `max_frac` are the lowest and
highest fractions with $|Z| > 2$. `min_net` and `max_net` show the range of
`up - down`. A change of sign means the balance of directions shifts.

```{r variable-genes}
# Rank genes by the range across seeds.
net_mat <- up_mat - down_mat
variation <- data.frame(
  gene = genes, top50_g = top50_g,
  min_frac = apply(frac_mat, 1, min, na.rm = TRUE),
  max_frac = apply(frac_mat, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE),
  min_net = apply(net_mat, 1, min, na.rm = TRUE),
  max_net = apply(net_mat, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
)
variation$range_frac <- variation$max_frac - variation$min_frac
variation <- variation[variation$top50_g > 0 & is.finite(variation$range_frac), ]
variation <- variation[order(-variation$range_frac, variation$gene), ]
rownames(variation) <- NULL
head(variation[, c("gene", "top50_g", "min_frac", "max_frac",
                   "range_frac", "min_net", "max_net")], 10)

# The most variable gene is used again in later sections.
variable_gene <- variation$gene[1]
```

We call `r variable_gene` the variable gene: among genes that entered the top
50 at least once, it has the largest change in the fraction of patches with
$|Z| > 2$ across seeds. The next maps show its meta Z scores.

```{r variable-gene-map, fig.width=18, fig.height=10, fig.cap=paste0(variable_gene, " meta Z scores. Each seed has its own color scale. Black borders mark the lowest and highest fractions with absolute Z above 2.")}
variable_frac <- frac_mat[match(variable_gene, genes), ]
low_seed <- which.min(variable_frac)
high_seed <- which.max(variable_frac)

# Show strong patches clearly and mark the two extreme runs.
seed_maps <- function(zlist) {
  variable_map <- gene_map(variable_gene, zlist)
  lapply(seq_along(seeds), function(i) {
  seed <- as.character(seeds[i])
  map <- variable_map[variable_map$seed == seed, ]
  frac_i <- mean(abs(zlist[[seed]][variable_gene, ]) > 2, na.rm = TRUE)
  limit <- max(2, abs(map$z), na.rm = TRUE)
  tag <- if (i == low_seed) " low" else if (i == high_seed) " high" else ""
  edge <- if (nzchar(tag)) "black" else "grey80"
  ggplot(map, aes(x, y, color = z)) +
    geom_point(aes(alpha = abs(z) > 2), size = 0.12) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(xy_use[, 1]), ylim = range(xy_use[, 2])) +
    scale_color_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "white", high = "#D55E00",
                          midpoint = 0, limits = c(-limit, limit),
                          breaks = c(-limit, 0, limit),
                          labels = round(c(-limit, 0, limit), 1),
                          na.value = "grey80", name = "Z",
                          guide = guide_colorbar(barwidth = grid::unit(2, "cm"),
                                                 barheight = grid::unit(0.15, "cm"),
                                                 title.position = "top")) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.25, `TRUE` = 1),
                       na.value = 0.6, guide = "none") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = edge, fill = NA,
                                      linewidth = if (nzchar(tag)) 1.1 else 0.3),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 6)) +
    labs(title = paste0(seed, ": ", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * frac_i), tag))
  })
}
wrap_plots(seed_maps(meta_z), ncol = 5)
```

For `r variable_gene`, the fraction of patches with $|Z| > 2$ ranges from
`r sprintf("%.2f", variation$min_frac[1])` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", variation$max_frac[1])` across seeds. Panel titles give this
fraction for each seed. Black borders mark the lowest and highest runs (by
meta Z). Patches with $|Z| \leq 2$ are faded. Each panel has its own Z scale;
use its legend to read the color values.

The same maps with raw Z scores show where the variation starts. Borders mark
the same two runs as above.

```{r variable-gene-map-raw, fig.width=18, fig.height=10, fig.cap=paste0(variable_gene, " raw Z scores. Same layout as the meta Z maps above.")}
wrap_plots(seed_maps(raw_z), ncol = 5)
```

If the raw maps already differ between runs, the variation comes from the patch
assignment. If the raw maps have only a few strong patches but the meta maps
have large strong areas, the meta analysis spreads these few patches to their
neighbors. Section [Raw and meta Z scores of `r variable_gene`](#variable-raw-meta)
checks this patch by patch.

```{r variable-gene-distribution, fig.width=18, fig.height=6, fig.cap=paste0(variable_gene, " meta Z scores across seeds. Red lines mark Z = -2 and Z = 2.")}
# Use one Z score per retained patch.
z_dist <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(seeds), function(i) {
  data.frame(seed = as.character(seeds[i]),
             z = as.numeric(meta_z[[i]][variable_gene, ]))
}))
z_dist <- z_dist[is.finite(z_dist$z), ]
z_dist$seed <- factor(z_dist$seed, levels = as.character(seeds))

ggplot(z_dist, aes(z)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~seed, ncol = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Patch Z score", y = "Number of patches")
```

Each panel is the histogram of the meta Z scores of `r variable_gene` across
retained patches in one run. Seed `r as.character(seeds[high_seed])` has the most patches
outside the red lines, and seed `r as.character(seeds[low_seed])` has the fewest.

# Raw and meta Z scores

The results above use meta Z scores. `patchDE()` gives a raw Z score for each
patch from its own cells. `patchMetaAnalysis()` combines this estimate with
those of the 10 nearest patches in W space and gives the meta Z score.
Comparing the two shows where the variation across seeds comes from. If raw Z
already varies, the variation comes from the patch assignment. If only meta Z
varies, it comes from the meta analysis.

We compare the two scores in three steps:

1. all genes in one run: how the meta analysis changes each Z score;
2. all genes across runs ([Agreement across seeds](#agreement-across-seeds)):
   how stable each gene's map is, for raw and meta Z;
3. one gene, `r variable_gene`, patch by patch.

```{r raw-meta-counts}
# Fraction of gene and patch pairs with |Z| > 2 in each run.
z_counts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(meta_z), function(seed) {
  data.frame(seed = seed,
             raw_Z2 = mean(abs(raw_z[[seed]]) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
             meta_Z2 = mean(abs(meta_z[[seed]]) > 2, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
z_counts
```

`raw_Z2` and `meta_Z2` are the fractions of gene and patch pairs with
$|Z| > 2$. Meta Z gives more such pairs than raw Z in every run. For
reference, a standard normal Z has $|Z| > 2$ with probability
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 200 * pnorm(-2))`. Section
[Null calibration](#null-calibration) measures this fraction in null runs of
these data.

The scatter plot below shows each gene and patch pair in one run. Points on the
grey diagonal have the same raw and meta Z. Points that move away from it
vertically are changed by the neighbor patches.

```{r raw-meta-scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Raw and meta Z scores for one seed. Each point is a gene and patch pair. Dashed lines mark Z = -2 and Z = 2."}
s1 <- names(meta_z)[1]
stopifnot(identical(dimnames(raw_z[[s1]]), dimnames(meta_z[[s1]])))
sc <- data.frame(raw = as.numeric(raw_z[[s1]]),
                 meta = as.numeric(meta_z[[s1]]))
sc <- sc[is.finite(sc$raw) & is.finite(sc$meta), ]
ggplot(sc, aes(raw, meta)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 80) +
  geom_abline(color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Seed", s1), x = "Raw Z", y = "Meta Z", fill = "Pairs")
```

## Agreement across seeds

We map each run's Z scores to cells. For each gene, we compute the
correlation of cell Z scores between every pair of runs and take the mean of
the `r choose(length(seeds), 2)` pairs. A value near 1 means the gene's map changes little across seeds.

```{r cell-agreement}
# Cell by seed matrix of Z scores for one gene. Excluded cells are NA.
cell_z <- function(zlist, gene) {
  vapply(names(zlist), function(seed) {
    z <- zlist[[seed]]
    as.numeric(z[gene, match(as.character(filtered[[seed]]), colnames(z))])
  }, numeric(nrow(xy_use)))
}
seed_cor <- function(zlist) {
  vapply(genes, function(g) {
    r <- suppressWarnings(cor(cell_z(zlist, g), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    mean(r[upper.tri(r)], na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
}
raw_top50 <- lapply(raw_z, function(z) {
  score <- rowMeans(abs(z) > 2, na.rm = TRUE)
  head(names(score)[order(-score, names(score), na.last = TRUE)], 50)
})
agreement <- data.frame(
  gene = genes,
  raw_cor = seed_cor(raw_z),
  meta_cor = seed_cor(meta_z),
  raw_top50 = rowSums(vapply(raw_top50, function(x) genes %in% x,
                             logical(length(genes)))),
  meta_top50 = top50_g
)
summary(agreement[, c("raw_cor", "meta_cor")])
```

`raw_cor` and `meta_cor` are this mean correlation for raw and meta Z scores.
For raw Z, the mean correlation ranges from
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(agreement$raw_cor, na.rm = TRUE))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(agreement$raw_cor, na.rm = TRUE))` across genes, with a
median of `r sprintf("%.2f", median(agreement$raw_cor, na.rm = TRUE))`. For
meta Z, it ranges more widely, from
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(agreement$meta_cor, na.rm = TRUE))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(agreement$meta_cor, na.rm = TRUE))`, with a median of
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(agreement$meta_cor, na.rm = TRUE))`. Raw values are
high for most genes, because patches from two seeds share many cells and the
raw Z of a patch depends on its own cells.

```{r cell-agreement-genes}
agreement[agreement$gene %in% c(head(gene_summary$gene, 10), variable_gene), ]
```

The table shows the ten frequent top 50 genes and `r variable_gene`.
`raw_top50` and `meta_top50` count the runs, out of `r length(seeds)`, in
which the gene ranks among the top 50 genes. As in the previous section, genes
are ranked by the fraction of retained patches with $|Z| > 2$, computed from
raw or meta Z scores.

```{r cell-agreement-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Mean correlation of cell Z scores across seed pairs. Each point is a gene. Labeled genes are the ten frequent top 50 genes and the variable gene. The dashed line marks equal agreement for raw and meta Z scores."}
lab <- agreement$gene %in% c(head(gene_summary$gene, 10), variable_gene)
ggplot(agreement, aes(raw_cor, meta_cor)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey60", size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = agreement[lab, ], color = "#D55E00") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = agreement[lab, ], aes(label = gene),
                           size = 3) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Raw Z: mean correlation across seeds",
       y = "Meta Z: mean correlation across seeds")
```

Points below the dashed line are genes whose meta map changes more across
seeds than their raw map.

## Raw and meta Z scores of `r variable_gene` {#variable-raw-meta}

Each panel is one run. Each point is one retained patch, with its raw Z on the
x axis and its meta Z on the y axis. A point at the right has a strong signal
in its own cells. A point at the top has a strong signal after combining with
its neighbor patches.

```{r variable-gene-raw-meta, fig.width=18, fig.height=8, fig.cap=paste0("Raw and meta Z scores of ", variable_gene, ". Each point is a retained patch. Dashed lines mark Z = -2 and Z = 2.")}
vg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(meta_z), function(seed) {
  data.frame(seed = seed, raw = raw_z[[seed]][variable_gene, ],
             meta = meta_z[[seed]][variable_gene, ])
}))
vg$seed <- factor(vg$seed, levels = as.character(seeds))
ggplot(vg, aes(raw, meta)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~seed, ncol = 5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = variable_gene, x = "Raw Z", y = "Meta Z")
```

```{r variable-gene-counts}
# Patches with |Z| > 2 per run, for raw and meta Z.
vg_counts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(vg, vg$seed), function(d) {
  data.frame(seed = d$seed[1], n_patches = nrow(d),
             raw_Z2 = sum(abs(d$raw) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
             meta_Z2 = sum(abs(d$meta) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
             max_raw = max(d$raw, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
rownames(vg_counts) <- NULL
vg_counts
```

The table counts the patches with $|Z| > 2$ in each run. In seed
`r as.character(seeds[high_seed])`, `r vg_counts$raw_Z2[high_seed]` patches have
$|\text{raw } Z| > 2$, but `r vg_counts$meta_Z2[high_seed]` have
$|\text{meta } Z| > 2$; the largest raw Z is
`r sprintf("%.1f", vg_counts$max_raw[high_seed])`. In seed
`r as.character(seeds[low_seed])`, these counts are `r vg_counts$raw_Z2[low_seed]` and
`r vg_counts$meta_Z2[low_seed]`. When a few patches have large raw Z and many
more have large meta Z, the meta analysis spreads a few strong patches to their
neighbors. With fixed-effect meta analysis, one patch with a very large raw Z
can dominate every patch that uses it as a neighbor.

# Ensemble across seeds

Here we combine the `r length(seeds)` runs for each cell. Each cell gets the Z
score of its patch in each run. For each gene, we show three maps:

- **median raw Z**: the median of the cell's raw Z scores across runs;
- **median meta Z**: the same for meta Z;
- **meta agreement**: the fraction of runs in which the cell has a strong meta
  signal in the same direction as its median, that is $|Z| > 2$ and the same
  sign as the median meta Z. A value of 1 means every run finds a strong signal
  of the same sign at this cell. A value near 0 means the median comes from
  weak or mixed signals.

Each fraction uses the runs in which the cell was retained.

```{r ensemble, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, fig.cap="Ensemble maps. Columns show the median raw Z, the median meta Z, and the meta agreement, which is the fraction of runs with |meta Z| > 2 and the same sign as the median meta Z."}
ens_genes <- unique(c("Axin2", "Irf8", variable_gene))
ens_panel <- function(v, title, limits = NULL, diverging = TRUE) {
  d <- data.frame(x = xy_use[, 1], y = xy_use[, 2], v = v)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y, color = v)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.12) +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = title, color = NULL)
  if (diverging) {
    p + scale_color_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "white", high = "#D55E00",
                              midpoint = 0, limits = limits,
                              na.value = "grey80")
  } else {
    p + scale_color_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey80")
  }
}
ens_plots <- lapply(ens_genes, function(g) {
  m_raw <- cell_z(raw_z, g)
  m_meta <- cell_z(meta_z, g)
  med_raw <- apply(m_raw, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  med_meta <- apply(m_meta, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  agree <- rowMeans(sign(m_meta) == sign(med_meta) & abs(m_meta) > 2,
                    na.rm = TRUE)
  agree[!is.finite(med_meta)] <- NA
  lim <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(c(med_raw, med_meta)), na.rm = TRUE)
  list(ens_panel(med_raw, paste(g, "median raw Z"), lim),
       ens_panel(med_meta, paste(g, "median meta Z"), lim),
       ens_panel(agree, paste(g, "meta agreement"), diverging = FALSE))
})
wrap_plots(unlist(ens_plots, recursive = FALSE), ncol = 3)
```

# Null calibration

To interpret the fraction of $|Z| > 2$ pairs, we need its value when
expression is unrelated to X. We obtain it from null runs. Each null run
replaces X with a null version, keeps the expression and cell positions, and
repeats the full pipeline: patches, filtering, DE, and meta analysis.

We use two null versions of X:

- **shuffle**: X is shuffled across epithelial cells. The null X has no
  spatial structure, so this run tests the DE model on its own.
- **rot180**: the immune cells are rotated by 180 degrees about the tissue
  center, and X and the immune distance are recomputed from the rotated
  positions. The null X keeps the spatial clustering of the real X at a new
  position relative to the epithelial expression. This run tests the full
  pipeline with a spatially structured X.

A shuffle run near `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 200 * pnorm(-2))` shows that the DE
model is calibrated. The difference between the rot180 and shuffle runs shows
how many extra $|Z| > 2$ pairs a spatially structured X produces.

```{r null-setup}
# Add "flip_x" or "flip_y" for more null runs.
null_transforms <- c("shuffle", "rot180")
null_seed <- seeds[1]
center <- apply(xy, 2, function(v) mean(range(v)))
move_xy <- function(p, type) {
  p <- as.matrix(p)
  switch(type,
         rot180 = sweep(-p, 2, 2 * center, "+"),
         flip_x = cbind(2 * center[1] - p[, 1], p[, 2]),
         flip_y = cbind(p[, 1], 2 * center[2] - p[, 2]))
}

# Moran's I with row-standardized weights on 10 nearest epithelial neighbors.
nn10 <- FNN::get.knn(xy_use, k = 10)$nn.index
moran_I <- function(v) {
  z <- v - mean(v)
  sum(z * rowMeans(matrix(z[nn10], nrow = nrow(nn10)))) / sum(z^2)
}

null_inputs <- lapply(null_transforms, function(type) {
  if (type == "shuffle") {
    # Shuffle X across cells. Immune cells do not move.
    set.seed(null_seed)
    return(list(X = sample(X_use), min_dist = dist_to_immune))
  }
  imm <- move_xy(xy[is_immune, , drop = FALSE], type)
  # Same rule as X: immune cells among the 100 nearest neighbors. The pool
  # contains each query cell itself, so we take 101 and drop the first.
  pool <- rbind(as.matrix(xy[!is_immune, , drop = FALSE]), imm)
  pool_immune <- rep(c(FALSE, TRUE), c(sum(!is_immune), nrow(imm)))
  idx <- FNN::get.knnx(pool, xy_use, k = 101)$nn.index[, -1]
  list(X = rowSums(matrix(pool_immune[idx], nrow = nrow(idx))),
       min_dist = FNN::get.knnx(imm, xy_use, k = 1)$nn.dist[, 1])
})
names(null_inputs) <- null_transforms

x_check <- data.frame(
  X = c("real", null_transforms),
  mean = c(mean(X_use), sapply(null_inputs, function(n) mean(n$X))),
  sd = c(sd(X_use), sapply(null_inputs, function(n) sd(n$X))),
  moran_I = c(moran_I(X_use), sapply(null_inputs, function(n) moran_I(n$X))),
  cor_with_real = c(1, sapply(null_inputs, function(n) cor(n$X, X_use))),
  row.names = NULL
)
x_check
```

A suitable null X has a mean, SD, and Moran's I (spatial autocorrelation)
similar to the real X, and a correlation with the real X close to 0.

```{r null-runs}
# Same patching, filtering, DE, and meta analysis as the real runs.
run_pipeline <- function(Xv, min_dist, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fit <- getPatches(xy = xy_use, X = Xv, Z = Z_use, npatches = npatches,
                    n_iters = n_iters, log_iters = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  pd <- getPatchDiagnostics(xy = xy_use, X = Xv, patches = fit)$patch_diagnostics
  pd$min_dist <- as.numeric(tapply(min_dist, fit$patch, min)[as.character(pd$patch)])
  pd$mean_counts <- as.numeric(tapply(log_tot, fit$patch, mean)[as.character(pd$patch)])
  keep <- with(pd, patch[
    mean_counts > count_thresh & min_dist < dist_thresh &
      n_cells >= min_cells & is.finite(x_sd) & x_sd >= min_x_sd &
      !is.na(membership_stability) & membership_stability >= min_stability
  ])
  stopifnot(length(keep) >= 2)
  patch <- fit$patch
  patch[!(patch %in% keep)] <- NA
  de <- patchDE(y = y, df = data.frame(X = Xv), patch = patch,
                pearson = TRUE, tot = tot, verbose = FALSE)
  meta <- patchMetaAnalysis(DEobj = de, W = getPatchAttributes(Z_use, patch),
                            k = 10)
  mz <- meta$X$ests / meta$X$ses
  list(retained = length(keep),
       raw = de$X$ests[, colnames(mz), drop = FALSE] /
         de$X$ses[, colnames(mz), drop = FALSE],
       meta = mz)
}
null_runs <- lapply(null_inputs, function(n) {
  run_pipeline(n$X, n$min_dist, null_seed)
})

null_summary <- do.call(rbind, c(
  list(data.frame(run = paste("real, seed", null_seed),
                  retained = ncol(meta_z[[as.character(null_seed)]]),
                  raw_Z2 = mean(abs(raw_z[[as.character(null_seed)]]) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
                  meta_Z2 = mean(abs(meta_z[[as.character(null_seed)]]) > 2, na.rm = TRUE))),
  lapply(names(null_runs), function(type) {
    r <- null_runs[[type]]
    data.frame(run = paste("null", type), retained = r$retained,
               raw_Z2 = mean(abs(r$raw) > 2, na.rm = TRUE),
               meta_Z2 = mean(abs(r$meta) > 2, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
))
null_summary
```

`raw_Z2` and `meta_Z2` are the fractions of gene and patch pairs with
$|Z| > 2$; a standard normal Z gives `r sprintf("%.3f", 2 * pnorm(-2))`. The
shuffle run gives `r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$raw_Z2[null_summary$run == "null shuffle"])`
for raw Z and `r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$meta_Z2[null_summary$run == "null shuffle"])`
for meta Z. The rot180 run gives
`r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$raw_Z2[null_summary$run == "null rot180"])` and
`r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$meta_Z2[null_summary$run == "null rot180"])`,
and the real run gives `r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$raw_Z2[1])` and
`r sprintf("%.3f", null_summary$meta_Z2[1])`. The figure below shows the full Z
distributions.

```{r null-distribution, fig.width=12, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Z scores in the real run and the null runs. The black curve is the standard normal density."}
z_long <- function(z, run, stage) {
  z <- as.numeric(z)
  data.frame(run = run, stage = stage, z = z[is.finite(z)])
}
real_key <- as.character(null_seed)
null_z <- rbind(
  z_long(raw_z[[real_key]], "real", "raw"),
  z_long(meta_z[[real_key]], "real", "meta"),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(null_runs), function(type) rbind(
    z_long(null_runs[[type]]$raw, paste("null", type), "raw"),
    z_long(null_runs[[type]]$meta, paste("null", type), "meta")
  )))
)
null_z$stage <- factor(null_z$stage, levels = c("raw", "meta"))
ggplot(null_z, aes(z)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 0.25,
                 fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_grid(stage ~ run) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-8, 8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Z score", y = "Density")
```
